text:
jules: Follow-up from RFC review: I'm leaning toward a claims-first token model plus server-held delegation proofs. Token = compact claims (svc, tenant, scope, caps) + assertion_id when delegation is involved. Policy eval remains server-side. Pros/cons?
remy: Server-held proofs mean fewer token bits but add a lookup when delegation is used. How often will delegation happen in practice?
sophia: From telemetry ~5% of S2S calls cross project boundaries today. We can optimize that common path and only fetch proofs on mismatch.
jules: Exactly. Idea: use a local bloom filter per node to quickly test if assertion_id likely exists; if bloom negative, skip remote fetch. If positive, do fetch. Keeps avg latency down.
kai: Bloom filters are probabilistic; false positives would cause extra fetches, OK. But our tail latency is the real problem. How do we measure impact?
sophia: Prototype plan: LRU cache of resolved assertion->policy + a compact on-disk snapshot for warm restarts. Add a prometheus histogram for auth latency per route. Run load tests with synthetic delegation rate 5-20%.
maria: Migration: run "silent-accept" mode where auth service accepts v1 keys but also logs a migration hint header: x-auth-migration: v1-legacy-used. SDKs can surface a banner.
remy: We'll need an exchange endpoint: /token/exchange to mint v2 (claims-first) tokens from v1 with proof of possession. That endpoint should be rate-limited and require operator approval for bulk exchanges.
devops-bot: deploy-bot: schedule canary for /token/exchange in eu-central-1, flag=claims-first-exchange, rollout=5%.
jules: Auditing: shim/exchange mappings must be auditable without leaking secrets. Proposal: store only hash(original_key) + resulting claims + timestamp in audit store with strict retention (30d) and access controls. Sample analytics sampling 0.5-1% for full record.
kai: What about RBAC primitives? Role IDs vs capability sets? I'm for capability-first: policy language = allow|deny on verb:resource. Role IDs are aliases for convenience.
sophia: Agree. Also add a simple policy template for common patterns (org-admin, project-reader, svc-ingest-writer) so teams aren't writing many rules.
maria: TTL and rotation: default svc tokens = 12h, high-priv operator tokens = 1h + enforced rotation, delegation assertions = 15m. All tokens must support explicit revocation APIs.
remy: Edge-case: offline services that can't contact auth for proof fetch. Maybe token should include a proof blob for offline mode (signed by auth), but then we re-introduce token bloat.
js: (typo) jules: For offline heavy clients we can support a "proof_blob" optional field that contains a compact signed delegation token (JWS). It should be opt-in and flagged; exchange endpoint can mint that for allowed clients.
sophia: Here's a sample v2 token shape (compact JSON):```json
{
  "iss": "redwood-auth",
  "sub": "svc:batch-uploader",
  "claims_v": "2",
  "tenant": "t-8888",
  "scope": "project",
  "caps": ["write:uploads","read:meta"],
  "assertion_id": "a-9f3b",
  "exp": 1747300000
}
```
remy: Nice. On the SDK side: when a v1 key is used, SDK should emit a non-fatal warning and include x-auth-migration header so customers can see usage in console. Also provide a CLI command auth migrate-key --to-v2.
kai: Performance fallback: if cache miss rate for assertions > 1% p99 latency, we'll consider batching assertion fetches at the gateway for grouped requests.
maria: Security nit: ensure assertion_id + proof_blob are short-lived and signed with rotating keys stored in KMS/HSM. Also require mTLS for token exchange endpoint.
jules: Action items: 1) sophia + kai: build prototype LRU+bloom snapshot and perf test harness (due Wed). 2) remy + maria: migration CLI + audit retention policy draft (due Fri). 3) devex to add SDK warning + dashboard tile for x-auth-migration. 4) I'll draft the claim schema doc and policy template examples.
sophia: I'll open the design doc and include measurement plan + sample curl flows for /token/exchange. Example exchange call:```bash
curl -X POST https://auth.redwood.internal/token/exchange 
  -H 'Authorization: ApiKey legacy:abcd' 
  -d '{"requested_claims": {"scope":"project","tenant":"t-8888"}}'
```
remy: One more: add a feature flag for "require-assertion-fetch" so we can enforce proofs at runtime behind the flag during rollout.
jules: Good. We'll surface all telemetry in the infra review next Tue. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
